claim: Full-length Bruton's tyrosine kinase (BTK) has been refractory to structural analysis.
source: Full-length Bruton's tyrosine kinase (BTK) has been refractory to structural analysis.
evidence: This is a statement about the historical difficulty in obtaining structural data for full-length BTK, presented as established fact in the abstract.

claim: The nearest full-length structure of BTK to date consists of the autoinhibited SH3–SH2–kinase core.
source: The nearest full-length structure of BTK to date consists of the autoinhibited SH3–SH2–kinase core.
evidence: This statement describes the state of structural knowledge prior to this work.

claim: Crystals of full-length BTK were produced for the first time.
source: We have produced crystals of full-length BTK for the first time
evidence: The authors report producing crystals of full-length BTK, which is a primary finding of the study.

claim: Despite efforts to stabilize the autoinhibited state, the diffraction data from full-length BTK crystals reveal only the SH3–SH2–kinase core with no electron density visible for the PHTH–PRR segment.
source: despite efforts to stabilize the autoinhibited state, the diffraction data still reveal only the SH3–SH2–kinase core with no electron density visible for the PHTH–PRR segment.
evidence: This is a direct observation from crystallographic data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Cryo-electron microscopy (cryoEM) data of full-length BTK provide the first view of the PHTH domain within full-length BTK.
source: Cryo-electron microscopy (cryoEM) data of full-length BTK, on the other hand, provide the first view of the PHTH domain within full-length BTK.
evidence: This is a primary finding from cryoEM experiments reported in the manuscript.

claim: CryoEM reconstructions support conformational heterogeneity in the PHTH–PRR region wherein the globular PHTH domain adopts a range of states arrayed around the autoinhibited SH3–SH2–kinase core.
source: CryoEM reconstructions support conformational heterogeneity in the PHTH–PRR region wherein the globular PHTH domain adopts a range of states arrayed around the autoinhibited SH3–SH2–kinase core.
evidence: This is an interpretation of cryoEM data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Disassembly of the SH3–SH2–kinase core opens a new autoinhibitory site on the kinase domain for PHTH domain binding.
source: On the way to activation, disassembly of the SH3–SH2–kinase core opens a new autoinhibitory site on the kinase domain for PHTH domain binding
evidence: This is a mechanistic interpretation based on structural and functional data presented in the manuscript.

claim: The PHTH autoinhibitory interaction is released upon interaction of PHTH with phosphatidylinositol (3,4,5)-trisphosphate.
source: that is ultimately released upon interaction of PHTH with phosphatidylinositol (3,4,5)-trisphosphate.
evidence: This is a mechanistic interpretation based on structural and functional data.

claim: Membrane-induced dimerization activates BTK.
source: Membrane-induced dimerization activates BTK
evidence: This is a mechanistic conclusion based on structural and functional data.

claim: A crystal structure of an activation loop swapped BTK kinase domain dimer likely represents the conformational state leading to trans-autophosphorylation.
source: we present here a crystal structure of an activation loop swapped BTK kinase domain dimer that likely represents the conformational state leading to trans-autophosphorylation.
evidence: This is a structural finding with mechanistic interpretation.

claim: BTK is the target of ibrutinib (IMBRUVICA), the first-in-class covalent kinase active site inhibitor.
source: The TEC family kinase, BTK (Bruton's tyrosine kinase) is best known as the target of ibrutinib (IMBRUVICA), the first-in-class covalent kinase active site inhibitor used to treat chronic lymphocytic leukemia, mantle cell lymphoma, Waldenström's macroglobulinemia, and chronic graft-versus-host disease.
evidence: This is established knowledge about BTK and its clinical relevance.

claim: Ibrutinib is used to treat chronic lymphocytic leukemia, mantle cell lymphoma, Waldenström's macroglobulinemia, and chronic graft-versus-host disease.
source: the first-in-class covalent kinase active site inhibitor used to treat chronic lymphocytic leukemia, mantle cell lymphoma, Waldenström's macroglobulinemia, and chronic graft-versus-host disease.
evidence: This is established clinical knowledge about ibrutinib's therapeutic applications.

claim: The TEC kinases are the second largest subfamily of non-receptor tyrosine kinases in the human genome after the SRC family.
source: The TEC kinases are the second largest subfamily of non-receptor tyrosine kinases in the human genome after the SRC family (Yu and Smith, 2011; Mano, 1999; Smith et al., 2001).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: The TEC and SRC kinases share the SH3–SH2–kinase domain arrangement (the 'Src module').
source: The TEC and SRC kinases share the SH3–SH2–kinase domain arrangement (the 'Src module') (Figure 1a).
evidence: This is established knowledge about domain architecture, supported by Figure 1a.

claim: Structures of the autoinhibited SRC family kinases were solved in 1997.
source: Structures of the autoinhibited SRC family kinases were solved in 1997 revealing, for the first time, the compact arrangement of the SH3 and SH2 domains assembled onto the distal side of the catalytic kinase domain (Xu et al., 1997).
evidence: This is historical information about SRC kinase structures, supported by citation.

claim: 18 years passed between the solution of autoinhibited SRC kinase structures and the first autoinhibited structure of a TEC kinase.
source: Despite the shared 'Src module' of the SRC and TEC families, 18 years passed before an autoinhibited structure of one of the TEC kinases was resolved by X-ray crystallography.
evidence: This is a historical observation about the timeline of structural biology studies.

claim: In 2015, the BTK SH3–SH2–kinase fragment was crystallized.
source: In 2015, the BTK SH3–SH2–kinase fragment was crystallized (Wang et al., 2015).
evidence: This is a historical fact supported by citation.

claim: The BTK SH3–SH2–kinase fragment crystallizes as a domain swapped dimer.
source: This BTK fragment crystallizes as a domain swapped dimer; the SH2 domain opens to allow the B helix of one chain to pack against the β-sheet of the other chain.
evidence: This is a structural observation from previous work (Wang et al., 2015).

claim: One-half of the domain swapped BTK structure represents the current model for autoinhibited BTK.
source: One-half of the domain swapped BTK structure represents the current model for autoinhibited BTK and closely resembles the compact structure of autoinhibited SRC kinases (Figure 1b).
evidence: This is an interpretation of structural data from previous work, illustrated in Figure 1b.

claim: The autoinhibited BTK core closely resembles the compact structure of autoinhibited SRC kinases.
source: One-half of the domain swapped BTK structure represents the current model for autoinhibited BTK and closely resembles the compact structure of autoinhibited SRC kinases (Figure 1b).
evidence: This is a comparative structural observation.

claim: The SRC kinases contain a C-terminal tail that is absent in the TEC family.
source: The SRC kinases contain a C-terminal tail (absent in the TEC family) that, upon phosphorylation on a conserved tyrosine, binds to the SH2 domain in an intramolecular fashion to stabilize the autoinhibited Src module.
evidence: This is established knowledge about structural differences between SRC and TEC kinases.

claim: Upon phosphorylation on a conserved tyrosine, the SRC C-terminal tail binds to the SH2 domain in an intramolecular fashion to stabilize the autoinhibited Src module.
source: The SRC kinases contain a C-terminal tail (absent in the TEC family) that, upon phosphorylation on a conserved tyrosine, binds to the SH2 domain in an intramolecular fashion to stabilize the autoinhibited Src module.
evidence: This is established knowledge about SRC kinase regulation.

claim: BTK stabilizes the SH2 autoinhibitory pose via a conserved acidic side chain at the end of the kinase domain.
source: BTK instead stabilizes the SH2 autoinhibitory pose via a conserved acidic side chain at the end of the kinase domain (Joseph et al., 2017).
evidence: This is a mechanistic finding from previous work, supported by citation.

claim: The SRC kinases contain an N-terminal SH4-unique domain region that is intrinsically disordered and has not been resolved in available crystal structures.
source: The SRC kinases also contain an N-terminal SH4-unique domain region (Figure 1a) that is intrinsically disordered and has not been resolved in the available crystal structures.
evidence: This is established knowledge about SRC kinase structure.

claim: The SRC kinases are myristoylated or palmitoylated in the SH4 domain driving membrane association.
source: The SRC kinases are myristoylated or palmitoylated in the SH4 domain driving membrane association (Koegl et al., 1994).
evidence: This is established knowledge about SRC kinase membrane targeting, supported by citation.

claim: BTK contains an extended N-terminal region (PHTH–PRR) consisting of the phospholipid-binding Pleckstrin homology (PH) domain followed by a Tec homology (TH) domain and a long linker housing two proline-rich regions (PRR).
source: In contrast, BTK contains an extended N-terminal region (PHTH–PRR) consisting of the phospholipid-binding Pleckstrin homology (PH) domain followed by a Tec homology (TH) domain and a long linker housing two proline-rich regions (PRR) (Figure 1a).
evidence: This is a description of BTK domain architecture, illustrated in Figure 1a.

claim: The folded N-terminal PH domain of BTK has been crystallized revealing a binding site for inositol 1,3,4,5-tetrakisphosphate (IP4), the headgroup of its target phosphatidylinositol (3,4,5)-trisphosphate (PIP3) ligand.
source: The folded N-terminal PH domain of BTK has been crystallized (Baraldi et al., 1999) revealing a binding site for inositol 1,3,4,5-tetrakisphosphate (IP4), the headgroup of its target phosphatidylinositol (3,4,5)-trisphosphate (PIP3) ligand (Figure 1c).
evidence: This is established structural knowledge from previous work, supported by citation and Figure 1c.

claim: The crystal structure shows the TH domain bound to zinc and closely associated with the PH domain.
source: The crystal structure shows the TH domain bound to zinc and closely associated with the PH domain
evidence: This is a structural observation from previous crystallographic work.

claim: The BTK PHTH domain crystallizes as a homodimer, named for the preeminent structural biologist, Matti Saraste.
source: The BTK PHTH domain crystallizes as a homodimer, named for the preeminent structural biologist, Matti Saraste, who solved the first BTK PHTH structure (Hyvönen and Saraste, 1997).
evidence: This is established structural knowledge from previous work, supported by citation.

claim: The N-terminal PHTH–PRR domains account for over 30% of the BTK sequence.
source: The N-terminal PHTH–PRR domains account for over 30% of the BTK sequence.
evidence: This is a quantitative observation about BTK sequence composition.

claim: The BTK PHTH domain structure has been solved both as the isolated domain and in a construct where PHTH is covalently attached to the BTK kinase domain through a short tether.
source: The BTK PHTH domain structure has been solved both as the isolated domain and in a construct where PHTH is covalently attached to the BTK kinase domain through a short tether (Wang et al., 2015).
evidence: This is a summary of previous structural work, supported by citation.

claim: The tightly tethered structure revealed an interface between the PHTH domain and the N-lobe of the kinase domain.
source: The tightly tethered structure revealed an interface between the PHTH domain and the N-lobe of the kinase domain (Figure 1d)
evidence: This is a structural observation from previous work, illustrated in Figure 1d.

claim: The contacts in the tightly tethered PHTH-kinase structure are mutually exclusive with the contacts between the BTK SH3 and kinase domain in the autoinhibited 'Src module'.
source: but the contacts are mutually exclusive with the contacts between the BTK SH3 and kinase domain in the autoinhibited 'Src module' (Figure 1b) raising questions about whether both the SH3 and PHTH domain associate with the kinase domain simultaneously.
evidence: This is a structural inference based on comparison of two structures.

claim: Solution-based Nuclear Magnetic Resonance and hydrogen/deuterium exchange mass spectrometry (HDXMS) studies point to autoinhibitory interactions between the PHTH domain and the activation loop face of the BTK kinase domain.
source: At the same time, we conducted solution-based Nuclear Magnetic Resonance and hydrogen/deuterium exchange mass spectrometry (HDXMS) studies (Devkota et al., 2017; Amatya et al., 2019) that point to autoinhibitory interactions between the PHTH domain and the activation loop face of the BTK kinase domain (Figure 1e).
evidence: This is a finding from previous solution-based studies, supported by citations and Figure 1e.

claim: The mapped PHTH-kinase interface reflects intermolecular contacts that result upon addition of excess PHTH domain to the isolated BTK kinase domain (NMR) or comparison of full-length BTK with the SH3–SH2–kinase fragment (HDXMS).
source: In this case, the mapped interface reflects intermolecular contacts that result upon addition of excess PHTH domain to the isolated BTK kinase domain (NMR) or comparison of full-length BTK with the SH3–SH2–kinase fragment (HDXMS).
evidence: This is a description of the experimental conditions used in previous studies.

claim: BTK structural data to date support two poses for the N-terminal PHTH domain: PHTH domain landing on the distal face of the kinase domain N-lobe and PHTH domain binding to the activation loop face of the kinase domain.
source: Thus, the BTK structural data reported to date support two poses for the N-terminal PHTH domain: PHTH domain landing on the distal face of the kinase domain N-lobe (Figure 1d) and PHTH domain binding to the activation loop face of the kinase domain (Figure 1e).
evidence: This is a summary of previous structural findings, illustrated in Figures 1d and 1e.

claim: Mutations were introduced into the SH3–SH2–kinase core in an effort to stabilize the compact autoinhibited conformation.
source: Mutations were introduced into the SH3–SH2–kinase core in an effort to stabilize the compact autoinhibited conformation.
evidence: This is a description of the experimental approach used in this study.

claim: The crystallography reveals the same domain swapped dimer solved previously and no electron density is observed for the PHTH-linker residues.
source: Despite efforts to optimize the autoinhibitory conformation of BTK, the crystallography presented here reveals the same domain swapped dimer solved previously and no electron density is observed for the PHTH-linker residues.
evidence: This is a primary crystallographic finding from this study.

claim: SAXS and cryo-electron microscopy (cryoEM) analyses support a BTK autoinhibited state wherein the core SH3–SH2–kinase region adopts the compact monomeric form much like that observed in the early SRC kinase structures.
source: Further analyses using both small angle X-ray scattering (SAXS) and cryo-electron microscopy (cryoEM) support a BTK autoinhibited state wherein the core SH3–SH2–kinase region adopts the compact monomeric form much like that observed in the early SRC kinase structures.
evidence: This is a finding from SAXS and cryoEM experiments presented in this study.

claim: CryoEM allows the PHTH domain to be directly observed; the globular PHTH adopts a range of conformational states that surround but do not contact the core 'Src module'.
source: CryoEM allows the PHTH domain to be directly observed; the globular PHTH adopts a range of conformational states that surround but do not contact the core 'Src module'.
evidence: This is a primary finding from cryoEM experiments in this study.

claim: A redesigned tethered PHTH-kinase construct with a lengthened linker revealed another binding pose for the BTK PHTH domain on the BTK kinase domain.
source: To revisit the PHTH domain crystallographically, we lengthened and redesigned the tether between PHTH and kinase domains to provide greater conformational freedom between domains. The resulting crystal structure revealed yet another binding pose for the BTK PHTH domain on the BTK kinase domain
evidence: This is a structural finding from crystallography experiments in this study.

claim: Mutational analysis supports a regulatory role for the PHTH-kinase interface observed in the redesigned tethered construct.
source: and mutational analysis supports a regulatory role for this interface in the full-length kinase.
evidence: This is a functional finding from mutational studies in this study.

claim: A structure of a BTK kinase domain dimer reveals a potential arrangement of this domain undergoing trans-autophosphorylation following PIP3-mediated dimerization.
source: Finally, we have also captured a structure of a BTK kinase domain dimer revealing a potential arrangement of this domain undergoing trans-autophosphorylation following PIP3-mediated dimerization.
evidence: This is a structural finding with mechanistic interpretation from this study.

claim: Substitution of key residues within the SH2-linker sequence with proline (construct '4P') reduces the catalytic activity of full-length BTK compared to wild-type BTK.
source: The catalytic activity of the full-length BTK 4P variant, measured by autophosphorylation on Y511 in the BTK activation loop, is reduced compared to wild-type BTK (Figure 2b).
evidence: This is a functional finding from kinase activity assays, shown in Figure 2b.

claim: The melting temperature (Tm) of BTK 4P is 4°C higher than wild-type BTK.
source: In addition, the melting temperature (Tm) of BTK 4P is 4°C higher than wild-type BTK consistent with stabilization of the overall fold (Figure 2c, Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a biophysical measurement from thermal shift assays, shown in Figure 2c.

claim: The L390F mutation does not change the activity of full-length BTK but increases the Tm by 1.5°C compared to wild-type BTK.
source: We find the L390F mutation does not change the activity of full-length BTK but it does increase the Tm by 1.5°C compared to wild-type BTK (Figure 2b , c and Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a finding from kinase activity and thermal shift assays, shown in Figures 2b and 2c.

claim: The BTK 4P1F mutant shows a further decrease in autophosphorylation activity and 4.5°C increase in Tm compared to wild-type BTK.
source: We therefore combined the 4P and L390F mutations (BTK 4P1F) and observe a further decrease in autophosphorylation activity and 4.5°C increase in Tm (Figure 2b, c and Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a finding from kinase activity and thermal shift assays, shown in Figures 2b and 2c.

claim: Incorporation of ITK activation loop residues results in dampened loop dynamics that favor the autoinhibited conformation.
source: We have previously show that incorporation of these ITK activation loop residues results in dampened loop dynamics that favor the autoinhibited conformation (Joseph et al., 2013).
evidence: This is a finding from previous work, supported by citation.

claim: The activity of full-length BTK with the ITK loop substitution is low and the Tm is 2.5°C higher than wild-type BTK.
source: As expected, the activity of full-length BTK with the ITK loop substitution is low and we find that this sequence change also stabilizes the overall protein as the Tm is 2.5°C higher than wild-type BTK (Figure 2b, c and Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a finding from kinase activity and thermal shift assays, shown in Figures 2b and 2c.

claim: Targeted modifications within the SH2-linker region and activation loop of BTK result in stabilization of the autoinhibited conformation.
source: These data suggest that targeted modifications within the SH2-linker region and activation loop of BTK result in stabilization of the autoinhibited conformation.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the kinase activity and thermal shift data.

claim: The SH3–SH2–kinase fragment adopts a compact conformation while the full-length BTK protein is more extended according to SAXS analysis.
source: Consistent with the previous observations (Duarte et al., 2020; Márquez et al., 2003), the SH3–SH2–kinase fragment adopts a compact conformation while the full-length BTK protein is more extended (Figure 2d, e).
evidence: This is a finding from SAXS experiments, shown in Figures 2d and 2e, consistent with previous work.

claim: The 4P1F BTK mutations have no effect on the average conformation of the SH3–SH2–kinase fragment according to SAXS-derived structural parameters.
source: The SAXS-derived structural parameters (Rg and Dmax) suggest that, compared to wild-type, the 4P1F BTK mutations have no effect on the average conformation of the SH3–SH2–kinase fragment.
evidence: This is a finding from SAXS experiments.

claim: Ab initio shape reconstructions of the SH3–SH2–kinase fragment superimpose with the autoinhibited SH3–Sh2–kinase model derived from the previously solved structure (PDB: 4XI2).
source: Ab initio shape reconstructions superimpose with the autoinhibited SH3–Sh2–kinase model derived from the previously solved structure (PDB: 4XI2) (Figure 2e, top).
evidence: This is a finding from SAXS experiments, shown in Figure 2e.

claim: The volumes of both the ab initio envelopes of full-length wild-type and 4P1F BTK mutant are elongated.
source: In contrast, the volumes of both the ab initio envelopes of full-length wild-type and 4P1F BTK mutant are elongated (Figure 2e, bottom).
evidence: This is a finding from SAXS experiments, shown in Figure 2e.

claim: The full-length 4P1F mutant exhibits a somewhat more compact envelope (decreased particle dimension compared to wild-type full-length BTK) possibly consistent with the stabilized SH3–SH2–kinase core shifting the conformational preferences of the N-terminal PHTH–PRR region.
source: The full-length 4P1F mutant exhibits a somewhat more compact envelope (decreased particle dimension compared to wild-type full-length BTK) possibly consistent with the stabilized SH3–SH2–kinase core shifting the conformational preferences of the N-terminal PHTH–PRR region (Figure 2d, e).
evidence: This is a finding from SAXS experiments with mechanistic interpretation, shown in Figures 2d and 2e.

claim: The FL BTKsc construct produced diffraction quality crystals both in the apo form and in the presence of various active site inhibitors.
source: The resulting construct, referred to as full-length BTK with stabilized core (FL BTKsc) (Figure 3a), provided diffraction quality crystals (5–7 days at 4°C) both in the apo form and in the presence of various active site inhibitors.
evidence: This is a description of crystallization results.

claim: The highest resolution data collected for FL BTKsc was 3.4 Å in the presence of the GDC-0853 (fenebrutinib) inhibitor.
source: The highest resolution data collected (3.4 Å) was in the presence of the GDC-0853 (fenebrutinib) inhibitor.
evidence: This is a description of crystallographic data quality.

claim: The electron density derived from crystals of full-length BTK (FL BTKsc) defines the same domain swapped dimer observed for the previously solved structure of the BTK SH3–SH2–kinase fragment.
source: Despite efforts to stabilize the autoinhibited form, the electron density derived from crystals of full-length BTK (FL BTKsc) defines the same domain swapped dimer observed for the previously solved structure of the BTK SH3–SH2–kinase fragment (Wang et al., 2015; Figure 3b, c).
evidence: This is a primary crystallographic finding, shown in Figures 3b and 3c.

claim: A 16.9° rotation along residues 346–384 in the SH2 and SH2–kinase linker is observed for the domain swapped dimer structure solved here compared to that solved previously.
source: A 16.9° rotation along residues 346–384 in the SH2 and SH2–kinase linker is observed for the domain swapped dimer structure solved here compared to that solved previously (Wang et al., 2015).
evidence: This is a structural comparison between the new structure and previous structure.

claim: There is no PHTH domain density visible in the FL BTKsc crystal structure even after the structure is fully refined.
source: Notably, there is no PHTH domain density visible even after the structure is fully refined.
evidence: This is a crystallographic observation.

claim: The crystals of FL BTKsc contain the full-length BTK protein with no evidence of smaller BTK fragments.
source: To confirm that the crystals contain the full-length BTK protein and not a degradation fragment, we harvested, washed, and analyzed the crystals by sodium dodecyl sulfate–polyacrylamide gel electrophoresis (SDS–PAGE) (Figure 3d). The result shows the crystal is full-length BTK protein with no evidence of smaller BTK fragments.
evidence: This is a finding from SDS-PAGE analysis, shown in Figure 3d.

claim: Four of the five full-length BTK constructs with varying mutations/deletions within the long PRR containing linker crystallize in a manner identical to FL BTKsc, with no electron density observed for the PHTH domain.
source: Finally, we built five additional full-length BTK constructs with varying mutations/deletions within the long PRR containing linker between the PHTH and SH3 domains (see Materials and methods). We find that four of the five constructs crystalize in a manner identical to FL BTKsc, which contains the wild-type sequence in the PHTH–PRR region, and no electron density is observed for the PHTH domain in any of these crystals (one construct did not form crystals).
evidence: This is a summary of crystallization results for multiple constructs.

claim: The solvent content in the crystals of full-length BTK is high (67%).
source: The solvent content in the crystals of full-length BTK is high (67%) and crystal packing shows large solvent channels (Figure 3e).
evidence: This is a crystallographic observation, shown in Figure 3e.

claim: The previously solved PHTH domain structure can fit into the solvent channels of the full-length BTK crystals.
source: Given the absence of PHTH domain electron density, we asked whether the previously solved PHTH domain structure could fit into the solvent channels. Placing the PHTH structure at the N-terminus of the BTK SH3–SH2–kinase model shows that the PHTH domain is readily accommodated within the solvent channels of the crystal (Figure 3e).
evidence: This is a modeling exercise based on crystal packing analysis, shown in Figure 3e.

claim: The C-lobe G-helix portion of the PHTH/kinase interface mapped previously by solution methods appears inaccessible in the crystal packing.
source: The C-lobe G-helix portion of the PHTH/kinase interface mapped previously by solution methods (Amatya et al., 2019), appears inaccessible
evidence: This is an analysis of crystal packing and potential steric constraints.

claim: The activation loop and the portion of the N-lobe previously identified within the PHTH/kinase interface are accessible in the crystal packing.
source: while the activation loop itself and the portion of the N-lobe previously identified within the PHTH/kinase interface are accessible.
evidence: This is an analysis of crystal packing and potential steric constraints.

claim: It is possible that the PHTH domain mobility in the crystal is due to steric occlusion of the previously identified regulatory site.
source: Thus, it is possible that the PHTH domain mobility in the crystal is due to steric occlusion of the previously identified regulatory site.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the crystallographic results.

claim: BTK particles were nicely distributed in the raw cryoEM images.
source: BTK particles were nicely distributed in the raw images (Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is an observation from cryoEM data collection, shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: After several rounds of 2D classification, the 2D classes resembling the autoinhibited SH3–SH2–kinase core start to become visible.
source: After several rounds of 2D classification, the 2D classes resembling the autoinhibited SH3–SH2–kinase core start to become visible (Figure 4a, b, Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a finding from cryoEM data processing, shown in Figures 4a and 4b.

claim: An extra unstructured density mass positioned adjacent to the main SH3–SH2–kinase core and a globular density distant from the core are evident in the 2D classes.
source: An extra unstructured density mass positioned adjacent to the main SH3–SH2–kinase core in addition to a globular density distant from the core are evident in the 2D classes and were persistently present after discarding specific 2D classes and repeated 2D classification.
evidence: This is an observation from cryoEM 2D classification.

claim: Three of the four 3D classes from ab initio reconstruction were of sufficient quality to fit models of BTK SH3–SH2–kinase.
source: From ab initio reconstruction and refinement, four 3D classes were obtained (Figure 4—figure supplement 1); three of which (Classes 0, 1, and 3) were of sufficient quality to fit models of BTK SH3–SH2–kinase (Figure 4c–e).
evidence: This is a finding from cryoEM 3D reconstruction, shown in Figures 4c-e.

claim: The presence of the monomeric SH3–SH2–kinase region in all of the 3D reconstructions is significant as all BTK crystal structures to date have revealed a domain swapped dimer.
source: The presence of the monomeric SH3–SH2–kinase region in all of the 3D reconstructions is significant as all BTK crystal structures to date have revealed a domain swapped dimer with two polypeptide chains contributing to the autoinhibited conformation.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the cryoEM results in the context of previous crystallographic findings.

claim: Two of the three 3D reconstructions (Classes 0 and 1) show density possibly representing the N-terminal PHTH domain and adjacent PRR linker region.
source: Two of the three 3D reconstructions (Classes 0 and 1) show density possibly representing the N-terminal PHTH domain and adjacent PRR linker region (Figure 4c, d).
evidence: This is a finding from cryoEM 3D reconstruction, shown in Figures 4c and 4d.

claim: The PHTH domain structure fits into the extra globular density that sits outside of the SH3–SH2–kinase core.
source: The PHTH domain structure fits into the extra globular density that sits outside of the SH3–SH2–kinase core
evidence: This is a modeling result based on cryoEM density.

claim: In one cryoEM reconstruction, continuous density is observed from the SH3–SH2–kinase core to the globular domain.
source: and in one reconstruction, continuous density is observed from the SH3–SH2–kinase core to the globular domain (Figure 4c).
evidence: This is an observation from cryoEM reconstruction, shown in Figure 4c.

claim: The remote globular density is not visible in Class 3, but continuous unresolved density next to the SH3–SH2–kinase core is present possibly indicating the location of the PRR linker region.
source: The remote globular density is not visible in Class 3, but similar to Classes 0 and 1, continuous unresolved density next to the SH3–SH2–kinase core is present possibly indicating the location of the PRR linker region that is covalently connected to the SH3 domain (Figure 4e).
evidence: This is an observation from cryoEM reconstruction with interpretation, shown in Figure 4e.

claim: HDXMS data on wild-type, full-length BTK are consistent with an exposed PRR linker region surrounded by two globular folded domains (PHTH and SH3).
source: HDXMS data on wild-type, full-length BTK (Figure 4—figure supplement 2) are consistent with an exposed PRR linker region surrounded by two globular folded domains (PHTH and SH3).
evidence: This is a finding from HDXMS experiments, shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2.

claim: Deuterium uptake reaches its maximum at the earliest time points for peptides spanning the linker between PHTH and SH3 consistent with high solvent accessibility and the lack of a well-defined hydrogen-bonding network.
source: Deuterium uptake reaches its maximum at the earliest time points for peptides spanning the linker between PHTH and SH3 consistent with high solvent accessibility and the lack of a well-defined hydrogen-bonding network.
evidence: This is a finding from HDXMS experiments.

claim: The deuterium uptake curves for peptides derived from all other regions of BTK (PHTH, SH3–SH2, kinase domains) are consistent with folded domains.
source: In contrast, the deuterium uptake curves for peptides derived from all other regions of BTK (PHTH, SH3–SH2, kinase domains) are consistent with folded domains.
evidence: This is a finding from HDXMS experiments.

claim: Results from crystallography and cryoEM suggest the PHTH domain is not stably associated with the autoinhibited SH3–SH2–kinase core of BTK but instead samples a broad conformational ensemble.
source: Results from crystallography and cryoEM presented here suggest the PHTH domain is not stably associated with the autoinhibited SH3–SH2–kinase core of BTK but instead samples a broad conformational ensemble within the context of full-length BTK that may include transient interaction with the autoinhibited core.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the crystallographic and cryoEM data.

claim: The BTK fragment lacking the PHTH–PRR region is more active than the full-length protein.
source: As well, the BTK fragment lacking the PHTH–PRR region is more active than the full-length protein (Wang et al., 2015)
evidence: This is a finding from previous work, supported by citation.

claim: Mutation of specific surface exposed side chains within the PHTH domain (R133 and Y134) results in modest activation of BTK.

source: In the structure solved here (Figure 5c, left), the longer linker between domains allows the PHTH domain to bind to the β-strands of the kinase domain N-lobe instead of the C-helix-binding site defined previously (Wang et al., 2015).

claim: The guanidinium group of R171 participates in hydrogen bonds with the side chains of S453 and Q459 in the kinase domain.
source: The guanidinium group of R171 participates in hydrogen bonds with the side chains of S453 and Q459 in the kinase domain (Figure 5d).

claim: The hydrophobic methylene groups of the R133 side chain contact I397 and Y461.

source: The 22-residue GS linker is only partially visible and is not involved in the PHTH–KD interaction.

source: The total solvent-excluded surface area of the PH–KD interface is 753.8 Å2.
evidence: This is a quantitative structural measurement.

claim: Neither the single mutations nor the double R133E/Y134E mutation alter the rate of the kinase reaction in the PHTH–kinase construct.
source: The data for the PHTH–kinase construct show that neither the single mutations nor the double R133E/Y134E mutation alter the rate of the kinase reaction (Figure 6b) or the time to 3000 pmol ADP (Figure 6c).

claim: Mutation of all three PHTH domain side chains (R133E/Y134E/R171E) increases BTK activity in the PHTH-kinase construct.
source: In contrast, mutation of all three PHTH domain side chains (R133E/Y134E/R171E) increases BTK activity (Figure 6a, b) and shortens the time to 3000 pmol ADP (Figure 6c).
evidence: This is a finding from kinase activity assays, shown in Figures 6a, 6b, and 6c.

claim: The interface captured in the loosely tethered crystal structure serves an inhibitory role at least in the tethered PHTH–kinase complex.
source: These data are consistent with the conclusion that the interface captured in the crystal structure serves an inhibitory role at least in the tethered PHTH–kinase complex.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the kinase activity data.

claim: Disrupting the PHTH/kinase interface (R133E/Y134E/R171E) results in a slight increase in the activity of full-length BTK.
source: Comparing the activity of wild-type full-length BTK to the R133E/Y134E/R171E mutant, we find that disrupting the PHTH/kinase interface results in a slight increase in the activity of full-length BTK (Figure 6d, e).
evidence: This is a finding from kinase activity assays, shown in Figures 6d and 6e.

claim: Mutation of W251K in the SH3 domain of full-length BTK leads to an increase in BTK activity similar to that of the R133E/Y134E/R171E mutation.
source: Mutation of W251K in the SH3 domain of full-length BTK by itself leads to an increase in BTK activity similar to that of the R133E/Y134E/R171E mutation (Figure 6d, e).
evidence: This is a finding from kinase activity assays, shown in Figures 6d and 6e.

claim: Mutation of W251 to lysine in combination with the R133E/Y134E/R171E mutation results in a more active kinase compared to constructs in which the autoinhibitory SH3 domain is intact.
source: Mutation of W251 to lysine in combination with the R133E/Y134E/R171E mutation results in a more active kinase (Figure 6d, e) and shorter time to the threshold ADP level (Figure 6f) compared to constructs in which the autoinhibitory SH3 domain is intact.
evidence: This is a finding from kinase activity assays, shown in Figures 6d, 6e, and 6f.

claim: The PHTH/kinase interaction and the SH3/SH2-linker/N-lobe contacts are mutually exclusive.
source: These data are consistent with the idea that the PHTH/kinase interaction and the SH3/SH2-linker/N-lobe contacts are mutually exclusive
evidence: This is an interpretation of the kinase activity data.

claim: Both the PHTH/kinase interaction and the SH3/SH2-linker/N-lobe contacts separately serve to allosterically inhibit the catalytic activity of the BTK kinase domain likely via stabilization of the hydrophobic stack.
source: and that both interactions separately serve to allosterically inhibit the catalytic activity of the BTK kinase domain likely via stabilization of the hydrophobic stack.
evidence: This is a mechanistic interpretation of the kinase activity data.

claim: Wild-type BTK and the active R133E/Y134E/R171E/W251K BTK mutant are both activated in the presence of PIP3 liposomes compared to liposomes that do not contain PIP3.
source: We find that wild-type BTK and the active R133E/Y134E/R171E/W251K BTK mutant are both activated (Figure 6g, h) and reach threshold ADP levels more rapidly (Figure 6i) in the presence of PIP3 liposomes compared to liposomes that do not contain PIP3.
evidence: This is a finding from kinase activity assays with liposomes, shown in Figures 6g, 6h, and 6i.

claim: Compared to wild-type BTK, the activating mutations in the PHTH domain (R133E/Y134E/R171E) result in increased activity even in the presence of PIP3.
source: Moreover, compared to wild-type BTK, the activating mutations in the PHTH domain (R133E/Y134E/R171E) result in increased activity even in the presence of PIP3 (Figure 6g, h).
evidence: This is a finding from kinase activity assays with liposomes, shown in Figures 6g and 6h.

claim: The autoinhibitory effect of the PHTH domain is detected both in the context of non-membrane-associated BTK and when BTK is activated by PIP3 binding to the PHTH domain.
source: Thus, the autoinhibitory effect of the PHTH domain is detected both in the context of non-membrane-associated BTK and when BTK is activated by PIP3 binding to the PHTH domain.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the kinase activity data with and without PIP3.

claim: The BTK kinase domain forms a face-to-face dimer in the crystal with two intermolecular interfaces.
source: The kinase domain forms a face-to-face dimer in the crystal (Figure 7a) with two intermolecular interfaces; the β3/C-helix loop in the N-lobe forms one interface (Figure 7b) and the domain swapped activation loop and G-helix mediate an extensive interface between the C-lobes (Figure 7c).
evidence: This is a structural observation from crystallography, shown in Figures 7a, 7b, and 7c.

claim: In the kinase domain dimer, the C-helix adopts an intermediate conformation between the previously solved active BTK kinase domain with the C-helix 'in' state and the inactive structure of the BTK kinase domain with C-helix 'out'.
source: In the N-lobe, the C-helix adopts an intermediate conformation between the previously solved active BTK kinase domain (PDB: 3K54) with the C-helix 'in' state and the inactive structure of the BTK kinase domain (PDB: 3GEN) with C-helix 'out'.
evidence: This is a structural observation with comparison to previous structures.

claim: The activation loop of one monomer in the face-to-face BTK dimer structure extends into the active site of the other monomer but electron density is missing for residues 546–559, which includes the Y551 autophosphorylation site.
source: The activation loop of one monomer in the face-to-face BTK dimer structure extends into the active site of the other monomer but electron density is missing for residues 546–559, which includes the Y551 autophosphorylation site (Figure 7d).
evidence: This is a structural observation from crystallography, shown in Figure 7d.

claim: Superimposing substrate-bound kinase structures onto the BTK kinase domain shows that Y551 from one BTK kinase domain monomer would easily reach a viable phosphor-acceptor position in the active site of the opposing monomer.
source: Nevertheless, superimposing two different substrate-bound kinase structures (tyrosine and serine phosphoacceptors) onto the BTK kinase domain (Figure 7d) shows that Y551 from one BTK kinase domain monomer would easily reach a viable phosphor-acceptor position in the active site of the opposing monomer.
evidence: This is a modeling exercise based on structural comparison, shown in Figure 7d.

claim: The swapped BTK dimer structure may represent a conformation along the trans-autophosphorylation activation pathway.
source: The swapped BTK dimer structure may therefore represent a conformation along the trans-autophosphorylation activation pathway (Beenstock et al., 2016).
evidence: This is a mechanistic interpretation of the structural data.

claim: The canonical Lys/Glu salt bridge with active kinase domains does not form in the BTK kinase domain dimer due to the unusual conformation of the phenylalanine side of the DFG motif (F540).
source: The canonical Lys/Glu salt bridge with active kinase domains does not form in the BTK kinase domain dimer due to the unusual conformation of the phenylalanine side of the DFG motif (F540) (Figure 7e).
evidence: This is a structural observation, shown in Figure 7e.

claim: The F540 side chain intercalates between the Lys/Glu side chains adopting what has previously been termed 'DFG-up' or 'DFGinter'.
source: The F540 side chain intercalates between the Lys/Glu side chains adopting what has previously been termed 'DFG-up' (Dodson et al., 2010; Colombano et al., 2019) or 'DFGinter' (Modi and Dunbrack, 2019).
evidence: This is a structural observation with reference to previous nomenclature, supported by citations.

claim: The C-helix is held in an intermediate state between the C-helix in and C-helix out conformations associated with active and inactive kinases, respectively.
source: The C-helix is therefore held in an intermediate state between the C-helix in and C-helix out conformations associated with active and inactive kinases, respectively.
evidence: This is a structural observation with mechanistic interpretation.

claim: D539 of the DFG motif points inward, orientated approximately 180° opposite from that in the DFG-in conformation of the active kinase.
source: In addition to the unusual position of F540, D539 of the DFG motif points inward, orientated approximately 180° opposite from that in the DFG-in conformation of the active kinase
evidence: This is a structural observation.

claim: E445 on the C-helix forms a hydrogen bond with the backbone amide of G541 in the DFG motif instead of forming a salt bridge with K430.
source: and E445 on the C-helix forms a hydrogen bond with the backbone amide of G541 in the DFG motif instead of forming a salt bridge with K430 (Figure 7e).
evidence: This is a structural observation, shown in Figure 7e.

claim: The active BTK structure shows close packing between the top of the R-spine and W395, which adopts the rotamer conformation required for active BTK.
source: The active BTK structure shows close packing between the top of the R-spine and W395, which adopts the rotamer conformation required for active BTK (Joseph et al., 2010).

source: The 'DFG-up' configuration in the kinase domain dimer structure is accompanied by the W395 rotamer that is associated with active BTK (Figure 7f).
evidence: This is a structural observation, shown in Figure 7f.

evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the structural data.

source: In fact, a previous structure of another TEC family kinase, BMX, reveals the same DFG-up state and the kinase domain in that case is also bound to dasatinib (Muckelbauer et al., 2011).
evidence: This is a comparison with previous structural work, supported by citation.

claim: Missing electron density in crystals of full-length BTK, elongated SAXS envelopes, and visualization of the PHTH domain by cryoEM support a model where the N-terminal BTK PHTH domain populates a conformational ensemble surrounding the compact/autoinhibited SH3–SH2–kinase core.
source: The findings reported here provide new insights into autoinhibition and allosteric control of the full-length, multidomain BTK protein. The data advance our understanding of BTK regulation as many previous studies did not interrogate the structure of the entire full-length protein. In pursuing full-length BTK, we find that missing electron density in crystals of full-length BTK, elongated SAXS envelopes, and visualization of the PHTH domain by cryoEM support a model where the N-terminal BTK PHTH domain populates a conformational ensemble surrounding the compact/autoinhibited SH3–SH2–kinase core (Figure 8a).
evidence: This is a summary interpretation of multiple experimental findings, illustrated in Figure 8a.

claim: Perturbations to the conformational state of the SH3–SH2–kinase core have no effect on the hydrogen/deuterium exchange behavior of the PHTH domain.
source: In previous work probing allosteric regulation of full-length BTK (Joseph et al., 2017), we consistently find that perturbations to the conformational state of the SH3–SH2–kinase core have no effect on the hydrogen/deuterium exchange behavior of the PHTH domain consistent with the dynamically independent PHTH domain observed here.
evidence: This is a finding from previous work, supported by citation, consistent with current findings.

claim: The autoinhibited state of full-length BTK features a conformationally heterogeneous PH domain that is connected to a compact core through a flexible linker and likely contacts the kinase domain only transiently.
source: Contrary to models of autoinhibited multidomain proteins where each globular domain is sequestered into a compact core, the autoinhibited state of full-length BTK might instead feature a conformationally heterogeneous PH domain that is connected to a compact core through a flexible linker and likely contacts the kinase domain only transiently.
evidence: This is a mechanistic interpretation of the structural and biophysical data.

claim: Similar conformational heterogeneity has been reported for the PH domains of phospholipases Cε and β.
source: Similar conformational heterogeneity has been reported for the PH domains of phospholipases Cε and β (Garland-Kuntz et al., 2018).
evidence: This is a comparison with previous work on other proteins, supported by citation.

claim: The BTK PH/kinase interface detected in solution studies masks the PIP3-binding site on the PH domain.
source: Like AKT, the BTK PH/kinase interface detected in solution studies masks the PIP3-binding site on the PH domain.
evidence: This is a finding from previous solution studies.

claim: Regulatory interactions between the BTK PHTH and kinase domains are transient.
source: However, consideration of all data to date suggests that regulatory interactions between the BTK PHTH and kinase domains are transient.
evidence: This is an interpretation based on all available data.

claim: Previously characterized contacts between the PHTH domain and the activation loop face or between the PHTH domain and the kinase domain N-lobe may all exist within the conformational ensemble of a range PH/kinase domain interactions.
source: Previously characterized contacts between the PHTH domain and the activation loop face (Amatya et al., 2019) or between the PHTH domain and the kinase domain N-lobe (Wang et al., 2015) may all exist within the conformational ensemble of a range PH/kinase domain interactions.
evidence: This is an interpretation that reconciles multiple structural findings.

claim: The N-terminal region of the SRC kinases has been invoked in 'fuzzy' intramolecular regulatory interactions with the Src module (SH3–SH2–kinase) core.
source: Non-PH domain containing kinases present similarly dynamic N-terminal regions that exert regulatory control over catalytic activity. The N-terminal region of the SRC kinases has been invoked in 'fuzzy' intramolecular regulatory interactions with the Src module (SH3–SH2–kinase) core (Arbesú et al., 2017).
evidence: This is a comparison with previous work on SRC kinases, supported by citation.

claim: The intrinsically disordered N-terminal regions of SRC increase the flexibility of the SH3–SH2–kinase core to promote ligand-binding interactions.
source: For SRC, it has been suggested that the intrinsically disordered N-terminal regions increase the flexibility of the SH3–SH2–kinase core to promote ligand-binding interactions (Pérez et al., 2013).
evidence: This is a mechanistic interpretation from previous work, supported by citation.

claim: Myristoylation of the N-terminal 'cap' region of ABL results in a key autoinhibitory contact between the N-terminal myristate and the ABL kinase domain C-lobe.
source: The N-terminal 'cap' region of ABL is another example of a long, disordered N-terminal region; myristoylation results in a key autoinhibitory contact between the N-terminal myristate and the ABL kinase domain C-lobe (Pluk et al., 2002; Nagar et al., 2003; Hantschel et al., 2003; Panjarian et al., 2013).
evidence: This is established knowledge about ABL regulation, supported by citations.

claim: The PRR in the linker between the PHTH and SH3 domains competes with the SH2–kinase linker for binding to the SH3 domain thereby shifting the conformational equilibrium of the autoinhibited core to a more open configuration.
source: Within BTK, we have previously shown that the PRR in the linker between the PHTH and SH3 domains competes with the SH2–kinase linker for binding to the SH3 domain thereby shifting the conformational equilibrium of the autoinhibited core to a more open configuration (Joseph et al., 2017; Laederach et al., 2002).
evidence: This is a finding from previous work, supported by citations.

claim: BTK SH3 displacement from the autoinhibited core via interaction with the PRR may be a prerequisite for the PHTH domain to take up the autoinhibitory pose on the kinase domain N-lobe.
source: Indeed, BTK SH3 displacement from the autoinhibited core via interaction with the PRR may be a prerequisite for the PHTH domain to take up the autoinhibitory pose on the kinase domain N-lobe defined here (Figure 8b).
evidence: This is a mechanistic interpretation based on structural and functional data, illustrated in Figure 8b.

claim: The SRC and TEC kinases seem to share dynamic regulatory features in their N-termini despite drastically different primary structures.
source: While these questions need further study, it is notable that the SRC and TEC kinases seem to share dynamic regulatory features in their N-termini despite drastically different primary structures.
evidence: This is a comparative observation about kinase regulation.

claim: The BTK hydrophobic stack residues, W421 and Y461, are a binding site for both the L390 side chain on the SH2–kinase linker and Y134 on the BTK PHTH domain.
source: Transition from fully autoinhibited to active BTK following receptor activation can be considered in light of the structural insights now available (Figure 8). The BTK hydrophobic stack residues, W421 and Y461, are a binding site for both the L390 side chain on the SH2–kinase linker (von Raußendorf et al., 2017; Figure 8a) and Y134 on the BTK PHTH domain (Figure 8b).
evidence: This is a structural finding from this work and previous work, illustrated in Figures 8a and 8b.

claim: Both the L390/hydrophobic stack interaction and the Y134/hydrophobic stack interaction allosterically inhibit BTK catalytic activity by stabilizing the inactive kinase domain conformation.
source: Both interactions allosterically inhibit BTK catalytic activity by stabilizing the inactive kinase domain conformation.
evidence: This is a mechanistic interpretation based on structural and functional data.

claim: Release of the regulatory SH3/SH2 domains opens the kinase N-lobe for secondary inhibitory interactions with the PHTH domain.
source: The SH3/L390/hydrophobic stack interaction is present in the autoinhibited Src module and release of the regulatory SH3/SH2 domains opens the kinase N-lobe for secondary inhibitory interactions with the PHTH domain (Figure 8b).
evidence: This is a mechanistic interpretation based on structural data, illustrated in Figure 8b.

claim: Once PIP3 is made available by the action of PI3K, the PHTH binds to PIP3 in the membrane and likely dimerizes through the Saraste dimer.
source: Once PIP3 is made available by the action of PI3K, the PHTH binds to PIP3 in the membrane and likely dimerizes through the Saraste dimer.
evidence: This is a mechanistic interpretation based on structural and functional knowledge.

claim: If the PHTH–kinase complex remains intact upon membrane association, electrostatic repulsion between the negatively charged BTK kinase domain and the negatively charged membrane surface might result in dissociation of the inhibitory BTK PHTH/kinase interaction.
source: If the PHTH–kinase complex remains intact upon membrane association (Figure 8c), electrostatic repulsion between the negatively charged BTK kinase domain and the negatively charged membrane surface might result in dissociation of the inhibitory BTK PHTH/kinase interaction and subsequent dimerization-mediated autophosphorylation in the kinase domain (Figure 8d).
evidence: This is a speculative mechanistic interpretation based on structural modeling, illustrated in Figures 8c and 8d.

claim: Mutation of the PHTH domain residues that contact the kinase domain led to more rapid PIP3-mediated activation of full-length BTK.
source: Indeed, mutation of the PHTH domain residues that contact the kinase domain led to more rapid PIP3-mediated activation of full-length BTK (Figure 6g–i) suggesting the PHTH autoinhibitory structure interaction might remain intact as BTK associates with PIP3.
evidence: This is a finding from kinase activity assays with liposomes, shown in Figures 6g-i.

claim: Grb2 association with the PRR of BTK results in higher levels of BTK activity at the PIP3 membrane possibly by destabilizing autoinhibited BTK.
source: This is consistent with a recent report that Grb2 association with the PRR of BTK results in higher levels of BTK activity at the PIP3 membrane possibly by destabilizing autoinhibited BTK (Nocka et al., 2022).
evidence: This is a comparison with recent work, supported by citation.

claim: The oncogenic p65BTK isoform lacks most of the PHTH domain and is expressed in colorectal carcinoma and some glioblastoma patients.
source: The autoinhibitory role of the PHTH domain in maintaining the BTK kinase domain in its inactive state until assembly at the membrane provides new insight into oncogenic forms of BTK. Specifically, the oncogenic p65BTK isoform lacks most of the PHTH domain and is expressed in colorectal carcinoma and some glioblastoma patients (Grassilli et al., 2016).
evidence: This is established knowledge about BTK isoforms in cancer, supported by citation.

claim: An extended transcript yields BTK-C, an isoform that contains additional residues at the N-terminus and is expressed in breast and prostate cancer cells.
source: As well, an extended transcript yields BTK-C, an isoform that contains additional residues at the N-terminus and is expressed in breast and prostate cancer cells (Eifert et al., 2013; Wang et al., 2021).
evidence: This is established knowledge about BTK isoforms in cancer, supported by citations.

claim: It is possible that the altered PHTH domain sequences in oncogenic BTK isoforms may contribute to oncogenicity by disrupting the autoinhibitory function of the PHTH domain.
source: In addition to effects on PIP3 binding, and/or interactions with other regulatory proteins, it is also possible that the altered PHTH domain sequences may contribute to oncogenicity by disrupting the autoinhibitory function of the PHTH domain.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation about the mechanism of oncogenic BTK isoforms.

claim: A model where the primary autoinhibitory contacts are housed within the SH3–SH2–kinase core is consistent with the fact that the SRC kinases lack the PH domain entirely and rely only on their SH3 and SH2 domains for autoinhibition.
source: A model where the primary autoinhibitory contacts are housed within the SH3–SH2–kinase core is consistent with the fact that the SRC kinases lack the PH domain entirely and rely only on their SH3 and SH2 domains for autoinhibition (Shah et al., 2018).
evidence: This is a comparative interpretation with SRC kinases, supported by citation.

claim: The inherent conformational heterogeneity of the BTK PHTH domain suggests the possibility of multifaceted regulatory roles for this single domain.
source: Despite the temptation to assign a stable autoinhibitory configuration to the BTK PHTH domain, the inherent conformational heterogeneity of the BTK PHTH domain instead suggests the possibility of multifaceted regulatory roles for this single domain.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the structural and biophysical data.

claim: The length of the PRR linker between PHTH and SH3 domain varies across the TEC family.
source: It will be interesting to compare the TEC kinases in this regard. The length of the PRR linker between PHTH and SH3 domain varies across the family
evidence: This is a comparative observation about TEC kinase family members.

claim: The loops that mediate formation of the BTK PHTH Saraste dimer are absent in the PHTH domains of other TEC kinases.
source: the loops that mediate formation of the BTK PHTH Saraste dimer are absent in the PHTH domains of other TEC kinases
evidence: This is a comparative observation about TEC kinase family members.

claim: One TEC kinase, RLK/TXK, lacks the PHTH domain and instead contains an N-terminal region nearly identical in length to that of the SRC kinases.
source: and one TEC kinase, RLK/TXK, lacks the PHTH domain and instead contains an N-terminal region nearly identical in length to that of the SRC kinases.
evidence: This is a comparative observation about TEC kinase family members.

claim: Subfamily-specific differences in structure, dynamics, autoregulation, activation, and allostery are likely important for control of distinct signaling pathways in distinct cell types.
source: Subfamily-specific differences in structure, dynamics, autoregulation, activation, and allostery are likely important for control of distinct signaling pathways in distinct cell types.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation about the functional significance of structural differences.
